## Part A: Integrity scenarios: green, amber or red? (5 minutes, 20:25)

In class we vote on scenarios 1, 3 and 4 in a poll; scenarios 2, 5 and 6 are homework. For each scenario choose:

- **GREEN**: acceptable as described.
- **AMBER**: acceptable **only if** something is fixed or disclosed (say what).
- **RED**: research misconduct or a serious breach. Do not do it.

Write one sentence explaining your colour.

| # | Scenario | Colour | Why? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Three patients' day-3 fluid charts are lost. A resident "remembers roughly" what their balances were and enters values so the dataset is complete. | | |
| 2 | After seeing the results, the team removes two patients with "strange" fluid values because they weaken the association. The paper does not mention it. | | |
| 3 | The head of department did not take part in the study but asks to be last author "because it is my department". | | |
| 4 | (a) A nurse uses an AI chatbot to improve the English of the Discussion she wrote, checks every sentence, and states this in the Acknowledgements. (b) A colleague uploads the study spreadsheet (names and hospital numbers included) to a free public chatbot and asks it to "run the statistics". | (a) | |
| | | (b) | |
| 5 | A cohort of patients with sepsis like FLUID-ICU is published as three papers (mortality, acute kidney injury and ICU stay) in three journals, none mentioning the others. | | |
| 6 | Two paragraphs of a published review are copied word for word into your Introduction. The review is cited at the end of the paragraph, but there are no quotation marks. | | |

## Part B: Proposal builder 7: ethics, registration, feasibility and publication plan

**In class (20:30, 15 minutes):** the instructor fills in this worksheet live on the shared screen for the running example (a retrospective cohort of fluid balance and 28-day mortality in adults with septic shock in our ICU). You suggest answers in the chat.

**At home this week:** fill it in for **your own** proposal. It becomes Part 4 of your written proposal and slides 5 (ethics and feasibility) and 6 (publication plan) of your presentation. Everyone submits the written proposal and the 6 slides before 19:30 on the day of Session 8 (`Course/Assignment/proposal_brief.md`).

### B1. Ethics and consent
| Question | Your answer |
|---|---|
| Which ethics committee will review the study? What type of review do you expect (exempt / expedited / full)? The committee decides. | |
| Who are the participants, and can they decide for themselves when they become eligible? | |
| Who gives consent (patient / legal representative / deferred consent / waiver requested)? Use the ICU consent flowchart (Session 7 slides). | |
| Who takes consent, when and where? | |
| What are the risks and burdens for participants, and how are they minimised? | |
| Does the study need registration (trials: yes, before the first patient, in ClinicalTrials.gov or another WHO registry; systematic reviews: PROSPERO; observational: recommended)? | |

### B2. Confidentiality
| Question | Your answer |
|---|---|
| Which direct identifiers will you collect (if any), and why? | |
| How will each patient get a study code? | |
| Where is the key file (code to identity) kept, and who can open it? | |
| Where will the de-identified data be stored (institution-approved, password-protected)? | |

### B3. Feasibility check (tick and comment)
| ✓ | Question | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| ☐ | **Time:** realistic timeline (ethics 1–3 months, recruitment, analysis, writing)? | |
| ☐ | **Money:** budget headings named (staff time, materials/tests, publication fee)? | |
| ☐ | **People:** who collects data (nights, weekends), who analyses, protected time? | |
| ☐ | **Patients:** how many eligible patients did your unit see last year? How many can you realistically enrol? | |
| ☐ | **Data:** are the key variables recorded routinely? How much is likely missing? | |

Biggest feasibility risk: ______________________  One fix: ______________________

### B4. Publication plan (slide 6 of your presentation)
| Item | Your answer |
|---|---|
| Working title (from your PICO: design, I vs C, P, O; 10–16 words) | |
| Target journal (and a back-up), checked in DOAJ / NLM Catalog, with fees and licence known | |
| Reporting guideline (CONSORT / STROBE / STARD / PRISMA / SPIRIT / CARE) | |
| Registration needed? Where? (from B1) | |
| Authors (all four ICMJE criteria) and their roles (CRediT) | |
| Conflicts of interest and funding to declare | |
| Data-sharing statement (what, where, under which conditions) | |
| Conference where you would present an abstract first | |

**Structured-abstract skeleton.** One line each. Results are the results you *expect to report* (format, not numbers).

| Section | One line |
|---|---|
| Background | |
| Methods | |
| Results (expected) | e.g. "28-day mortality: n/N per group, RR (95% CI)" |
| Conclusion | Write the sentence you would use if the result is positive, and the one you would use if it is not. |

## Part C: Manuscript workshop 1: Methods and Results (45 minutes, 21:35)

### What you are doing
Each participant writes the **Methods** and **Results** of their own short STROBE-guided paper on **one FLUID-ICU question**, using **only** the results pack for that question. We give you the results; you write the paper. Nobody calculates anything.

| Question | Topic | Results pack |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Positive fluid balance by day 3 and 28-day mortality | `Course/Data/results_packs/Results_Pack_Q1` |
| Q2 | Cumulative fluid balance and acute kidney injury (AKI) | `Results_Pack_Q2` |
| Q3 | Cumulative fluid balance and ventilator-free days | `Results_Pack_Q3` |
| Q4 | Initial lactate and 28-day mortality; complete-case vs multiple imputation | `Results_Pack_Q4` |
| Q5 | Fluid balance and ICU length of stay among survivors | `Results_Pack_Q5` |

FLUID-ICU is a **simulated teaching dataset**. In your ethics sentence write: *"This analysis used a simulated teaching dataset; no ethics approval or consent was required."*

### How the 45 minutes are used
| Clock | Who | Task |
|---|---|---|
| 21:35–21:50 | Whole class, on Q1 | The instructor shares the template and results pack Q1. You suggest each Methods sentence in the chat; the instructor types the best one. |
| 21:50–22:02 | Whole class, on Q1 | Results: participants first, the Table 1 sentence, outcome numbers, crude and adjusted estimates. |
| 22:02–22:05 | Whole class | A volunteer reads every number in the class draft against the pack. |
| 22:05–22:20 | You, alone | Open the results pack for YOUR question. Follow the structure of the class draft and start your Methods. Ask questions in the chat. |
| At home | You | Finish the Methods and Results (~600 words), Table 1 and one figure or table. If you chose Q1, write it in your own words; do not copy the class draft. |

The class draft is shared as a PDF after the session.

### Methods: headings and checklist (STROBE items in brackets)
- **Study design and setting** (4, 5): prospective multicentre cohort; 4 ICUs; dates as given in the pack.
- **Participants** (6): who was included and excluded; how many.
- **Variables** (7): exposure (how fluid balance was calculated and over which days), outcome (definition and time point), confounders adjusted for.
- **Data sources** (8): routine ICU charts / study case report form.
- **Bias** (9): how confounding by indication was addressed (adjustment for severity).
- **Study size** (10): "all eligible patients in the cohort were included" (no new sample size for a fixed dataset).
- **Statistical analysis** (12): summary statistics; the test for each comparison; the regression model(s) and which variables; how missing data were handled; software (R, version from the pack); reporting of 95% CIs.

### Results checklist
- [ ] Participants first: number analysed (and excluded, with reasons) (13)
- [ ] Table 1 summarised in one or two sentences: how the groups differed at baseline (14)
- [ ] Outcome numbers per group (15)
- [ ] Main result: **crude AND adjusted** estimate with 95% CI (16)
- [ ] One further analysis (secondary outcome, sensitivity, imputation) (17)
- [ ] No interpretation ("because", "suggests", "important"). Move it to the Discussion
- [ ] No number without its unit and, for effects, its 95% CI

### Question-specific reminders
- **Q3:** ventilator-free days are skewed and count death as zero; choose the summary accordingly.
- **Q4:** report BOTH the complete-case and the multiple-imputation estimates.
- **Q5:** survivors only; use medians and IQR.

### Deliverable
Your own Methods + Results (~600 words) + Table 1 + one figure or table, saved as `Surname_Manuscript_QN_draft1` in the course folder (or sent by email) **before Session 8**. In Session 8 you add the Introduction, Discussion, Abstract and Title, and submit the complete draft by 23:59 that day (`Course/Assignment/manuscript_brief.md`).
